_note: One fact a day for the 'UK vs Jamaica' section (date-seeded permutation). source: worldbank | imf | who (code-fetched; a country the API lacks falls back to a domain-restricted AI web search) | search (AI web search only, of 'domains'). format: usd | pct | count | dec | index (3 decimals) | year; 'unit' follows dec values. 'harmonised': true only when one organisation publishes an internationally comparable series; otherwise no ratio or gap is computed ('not_compared_because' says why). 'stale_years' overrides the staleness warning age. 'geography' narrows what a searched figure must cover (default the whole country). who entries pin their dimensions in 'filter' and give their human 'page'. Editing this list mid-cycle reshuffles the rotation once.

facts.label: Government debt (% of GDP)
facts.meaning: What all levels of government owe, measured against one year of the country's total output.

facts.label: Unemployment rate
facts.meaning: The share of people available for and seeking work who don't have a job.

facts.label: Consumer price inflation (annual %)
facts.meaning: How fast the average prices of household goods and services rose over the year.

facts.label: GDP per person (current US$)
facts.meaning: Output per person: a rough gauge of average living standards, before adjusting for local prices.

facts.label: Money sent home from abroad (% of GDP)
facts.meaning: Personal remittances: money sent home by people working abroad, relative to the size of the economy.

facts.label: People using the internet (% of population)
facts.meaning: The share of people who used the internet in the last three months, from any device.

facts.label: People living in towns and cities (% of population)
facts.not_compared_because: each country uses its own definition of an urban area
facts.meaning: The share of the population living in areas each country's statistics office defines as urban.

facts.label: People aged 65 and over (% of population)
facts.meaning: How old the population is: the share of residents who have reached 65.

facts.label: Population density
facts.meaning: How many people live on each square kilometre of land, on average.

facts.label: Fertility rate
facts.meaning: The number of children a woman would have over her life at today's birth rates for each age.

facts.label: Life expectancy at birth
facts.meaning: How long a baby born that year would live on average if today's death rates at each age stayed the same.

facts.label: Adults living with obesity (%)
facts.meaning: The share of adults with a body-mass index of 30 or more, age-standardised so countries with older or younger populations compare fairly.

facts.label: Maternal deaths
facts.meaning: Women who die from pregnancy or childbirth-related causes, for every 100,000 babies born alive.

facts.label: Medical doctors
facts.meaning: How many practising medical doctors there are for every 10,000 people.

facts.label: Alcohol drunk per adult
facts.unit: litres of pure alcohol a year
facts.meaning: Recorded and unrecorded alcohol drunk in a year per person aged 15 or over, in litres of pure alcohol.

facts.label: Prison population rate (UK: England and Wales)
facts.not_compared_because: the UK figure covers England and Wales only
facts.meaning: How many people are held in prison (including those awaiting trial) for every 100,000 people. The World Prison Brief has no UK-wide figure, so the UK's is England and Wales, where most of its population lives.

facts.label: Homelessness (UK: England)
facts.not_compared_because: the two countries define and count homelessness differently
facts.meaning: How many people official figures count as homeless. The UK publishes no UK-wide figure, so the UK's is England's. Definitions differ a lot (from people sleeping rough to households in temporary accommodation), so compare with care.

facts.label: Year the present-day state was formed
facts.meaning: For the UK, the year the Acts of Union joined England and Scotland as Great Britain, the start of today's state; for Jamaica, the year it became independent.

facts.label: Human Development Index
facts.meaning: The UN's summary of a long and healthy life, education and income, from 0 to 1; higher means more developed.

facts.label: Intentional homicide rate
facts.meaning: Unlawful killings intended to cause death or serious injury, for every 100,000 people, as compiled by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime.

facts.label: Under-five mortality
facts.meaning: Children who die before their fifth birthday for every 1,000 born alive, as estimated by the UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation.

facts.label: Women's share of seats in parliament
facts.meaning: The share of seats in the national parliament's lower or single chamber held by women.
